Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about intelligence.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Intelligence is often said to be what intelligence tests measure. Evaluate what psychologists
have discovered about intelligence and include a discussion of psychometric testing. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you could test teacher accuracy in assessing giftedness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe different types and definitions of giftedness.

text: Children can be gifted in many ways. The problem is how to know whether they are truly gifted,
very good or just had a lucky day. You could ask a teacher for his or her opinion, but a different
teacher might give a conflicting view. What we need is a teacher consistency test!

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest one way in which Charlie’s motivation can be improved.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the assumptions of the approach to education on which your suggestion is based.

Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Chrissy has passed her examination achieving a grade A, but Charlie has failed his. Charlie is
demotivated and is considering giving up his studies.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘physiology of stress’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the general adaptation syndrome (GAS model) proposed by Selye. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about health promotion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“If we scare people enough they will change their behaviour.” Evaluate what psychologists
have discovered about health promotion and include a discussion of the ethics of health
promotions. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Devise a cognitive strategy for reducing acute pain that could be used by anyone.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain the theory that would enable your strategy to work.

text: If I’m in pain, such as when I trap my finger in a door, all I have to do is to think of my favourite
food, pizza, and the pain goes away!

parts.text: Suggest an appropriate way to observe the medical practitioner.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You have been invited to work as a researcher on non-verbal interpersonal skills in medical
practitioners. The research question is simply to discover which non-verbal skills the practitioner
you are observing uses most often.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘positive uses of sound (music)’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two studies which have investigated the effect of music on consumer behaviour.

Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about density and crowding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“Rats and humans: same or different ?” Evaluate what psychologists have learned about
density and crowding including a discussion of the usefulness of animals in psychological
research. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you might investigate differences between males and females in the errors they
make when drawing sketch maps.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Using examples, describe the types of errors typically made when drawing sketch maps.

text: It is said that women cannot read maps and make lots of errors using them. Is this true or not? As
psychologists we need to investigate before drawing any conclusion.

parts.text:
Describe the difference between alpha and beta personal space and describe the stop-
distance method.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you could investigate beta personal space using the stop-distance method to
gather qualitative data.

Answer this question.

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about models of abnormality.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
There are a number of different models of abnormality, each with strengths and weaknesses.
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about models of abnormality including a

Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Victor gets up at 4am to go to school because he has to wash and then wash again because
he does not feel clean. Then Victor washes again and again. Victor has obsessive-compulsive
disorder (OCD) which involves obsessions (thoughts) and compulsions (behaviours).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about the selection of people for work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“We want to give the job to the best applicant.” Evaluate what psychologists have discovered
about the selection of people for work and include a discussion of the strengths and
weaknesses of the interview method.

Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you can increase production and keep your workers happy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe goal setting theory by Latham and Locke (1984).

text: How can workers be motivated? Your organisation produces badges that say “I love psychology”
and the average worker makes ten every hour. You want to increase production, so you set a goal
for your workers.
